EV-ENEM-002 (error): Verified by reading enemy-pursuit-search-foundation, enemy-status-effect-displacement, and enemy-health-damage-defeat's existing reset acceptance/validation criteria (confirming the established pattern), then confirming melee-enemy, ranged-enemy, and locked-door-enemy-attack's full records contain no such criteria, and confirming floor-run-restart-persistent-closure's depends_on list omits all three keys. EV-ENEM-003 (error): Verified encounter-admission-cap-enforcement's three acceptance criteria (capacity query, delay/reduce-first, non-duplication) contain no reset entry point, despite floor-run-restart-persistent-closure already depending on it and the GDD explicitly naming 'encounter activation/admission state' as a required reset participant in both the Loss and Floor-run restart ownership paragraphs. Repaired by adding the missing reset acceptance/validation criteria; no dependency-edge change was needed since the edge already exists.

EV-ENEM-004 (warning, credible): Read the GDD's Loss and Floor-run restart ownership paragraphs directly — both state registry bookkeeping resets to 'the floor's initial state' with no mention of 'empty,' and the enemy-reset text separately requires each persistent enemy be returned to its authored spawn region and initial AI state (which could be active). active-enemy-registry's acceptance/validation criteria asserted an invented 'initial empty/starting state' and no criterion addressed the re-registration handoff with enemy-owned restart restoration. Repaired via remove_unique/append_unique pairs correcting the wording plus one new append_unique acceptance criterion covering the re-registration/consistency gap, keeping the fix on the registry (the natural bookkeeping-accuracy owner) rather than manufacturing a duplicate criterion on enemy-health-damage-defeat.

No findings were rejected — all four were independently verified as accurate against the GDD and the frozen candidate's actual field content before any edit was made. No new work items, features, or mechanics were invented; every change is a field-level acceptance_criteria/validation_requirements/depends_on correction on existing work items, consistent with the bounded stream-repair contract.

finding_resolutions.explanation: Confirmed against the frozen candidate: door-open-interaction's 5 acceptance criteria and encounter-admission-cap-enforcement's 3 acceptance criteria contain no reset-entry-point requirement, even though floor-run-restart-bootstrap and floor-run-restart-persistent-closure both depend on them specifically to invoke such an entry point, and every other named persistent owner (player-health, player-mana, player-movement, doorway-crossing-state, door-close-lock-break-lifecycle, active-enemy-registry, enemy-health-damage-defeat, enemy-pursuit-search-foundation, enemy-status-effect-displacement, fireball, frost-field, force-wave) does carry this criterion. Added an owner-side reset-entry-point acceptance criterion to each of door-open-interaction and encounter-admission-cap-enforcement per GDD Floor-run restart ownership, mirroring the phrasing already used on the other listed owners. Existing dependency edges are left unchanged since they become satisfiable once the owners are obligated to expose the interface.

Confirmed against the frozen candidate: final-escape-victory's depends_on entries for player-movement and door-open-interaction both justify the edge by a required owner-controlled suspend interface, but neither owner's acceptance_criteria contains that requirement, unlike fireball/frost-field/force-wave which already carry the matching criterion. Added a mirrored gameplay-enable/suspend acceptance criterion to player-movement (stopping already-active input-driven movement) and door-open-interaction (stopping an in-progress door approach/opening timer), each requiring rejection of new commands while suspended and re-enable only via an authorized reset/test flow, consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability. Existing final-escape-victory dependency edges are left unchanged.

repair.reasoning: Both supplied findings (STRUCT-001, STRUCT-002) are structural gaps of the same shape: a consumer's depends_on.reason asserts an owner must expose a reset or suspend entry point, but the named owner's acceptance_criteria never states that obligation, leaving the requirement enforceable only in the consumer's prose. I verified each claim directly against the frozen candidate's acceptance_criteria arrays for door-open-interaction, encounter-admission-cap-enforcement, and player-movement, and confirmed both findings' descriptions match the current record contents exactly (5 criteria on door-open-interaction, 3 on encounter-admission-cap-enforcement, 4 on player-movement, none containing a reset or suspend requirement). I also confirmed the mirrored pattern already exists on fireball/frost-field/force-wave (reset entry point + suspend interface acceptance criteria) and on player-health/player-mana/doorway-crossing-state/etc. (reset entry point criteria), so adding matching criteria to the three gap owners is a direct application of an already-established in-graph pattern rather than new invented design. No dependency edges, exclusive resources, or other fields needed changes — the fix is purely adding the missing owner-side acceptance criteria via append_unique, preserving every other field of these work items untouched.
